tasks.title: LEAF B1: session_gate: pure gate transition validation rules
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/session_gate.py is created as a NEW whole-file module.
Exposes gate_transition(rows, from_phase, to_phase) returning a structured GateResult(ok, error).
Enforces: hunt -> triage needs >= 1 valid Finding (deserialized and validated via Finding.validate()).
Enforces: triage -> poc needs unique/deduplicated findings.
Enforces: poc -> detonate needs every PoC.finding_id to map to an existing finding ID.
Enforces: detonate -> report needs every PoC finding ID to have a corresponding LiveTestReport.
Pure over rows list, no database or I/O access in session_gate.

spec.objective: Implement the pure transition gate validation rules for the pipeline phases.
functional_requirements: Implement GateResult dataclass with ok: bool and error: Optional[str] fields.
Implement gate_transition(rows, from_phase, to_phase) -> GateResult, where rows is a list of dictionary representations of Finding, PoC, or LiveTestReport contracts.
Validate hunt -> triage: check that there is at least one Finding, and that each Finding validates successfully via validate().
Validate triage -> poc: check that findings in the rows have unique IDs.
Validate poc -> detonate: verify that every PoC.finding_id corresponds to a valid registered Finding ID in the rows.
Validate detonate -> report: verify that every PoC (or finding) has a corresponding LiveTestReport.
spec.interfaces: GateResult(ok: bool, error: Optional[str]); gate_transition(rows: List[dict], from_phase: str, to_phase: str) -> GateResult
edge_cases: Empty rows list passed to gate_transition: returns GateResult(ok=False, error='No artifacts found')
Invalid severity value in a finding: validate() raises ValueError, caught to return GateResult(ok=False, error=...)
Multiple findings with duplicate IDs during triage -> poc transition: returns GateResult(ok=False, error='Duplicate findings detected')
PoC finding_id does not exist in findings during poc -> detonate transition: returns GateResult(ok=False, error=...)
PoC lacks a LiveTestReport during detonate -> report: returns GateResult(ok=False, error=...)
non_goals: Do not connect to SQLite database or perform file I/O in this module; the word integration is named here to specify this is a pure unit logic module.
spec.implementation_notes:
Create the module as ngv2/session_gate.py. Import dataclasses and ngv2.contracts (Finding, PoC, LiveTestReport). Keep the validation pure and clean.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.


# COMMITTED ORACLE CONTRACT (authoritative; you cannot read these files at synthesis time so they are reproduced verbatim -- your code MUST make them pass):

## tests/ngv2/test_session_gate_wired.py
```python
"""RED oracle for ngv2/session_gate.py (Agentic Spine Epic B, LEAF B1).

Pure transition-gate validators. NO database access in this module; the gate
operates over an injected, deserialized artifact set ("rows").

Pinned contract (the blind worker MUST build to this):

- ``gate_transition(rows, from_phase, to_phase) -> GateResult`` where
  ``GateResult`` exposes ``.ok`` (bool) and ``.error`` (str | None; None or ''
  when ok, a specific non-empty diagnostic when not ok).

- ``rows`` is a dict keyed by artifact type. Each value is a list of artifact
  *dicts* (the ``to_dict()`` forms of the contract dataclasses), which the gate
  deserializes via the contracts' ``from_dict`` and validates with each
  artifact's ``validate()``. Chosen shape::

      {
          'findings': [Finding.to_dict(), ...],
          'pocs':     [PoC.to_dict(), ...],
          'reports':  [LiveTestReport.to_dict(), ...],
      }

  Missing keys are treated as empty lists.

Gate rules (the four pipeline edges):

- ``hunt -> triage``   : ok iff there is >= 1 valid ``Finding``.
- ``triage -> poc``    : ok iff the findings are deduped (no duplicate
                          ``Finding.id``) and >= 1 finding exists.
- ``poc -> detonate``  : ok iff every ``PoC.finding_id`` maps to a registered
                          finding id (no orphan PoC).
- ``detonate -> report``: ok iff every PoC has a matching ``LiveTestReport``
                          (i.e. some report.poc_finding_id == poc.finding_id).
"""
import pytest

from ngv2.contracts import Finding, PoC, LiveTestReport
from ngv2.session_gate import gate_transition, GateResult


def _finding(fid="F1", severity="high"):
    return Finding(
        id=fid,
        target="svc.example",
        category="injection",
        severity=severity,
        title="title-" + fid,
        description="desc-" + fid,
        evidence=[],
    ).to_dict()


def _poc(finding_id="F1"):
    return PoC(
        finding_id=finding_id,
        language="python",
        code="print('x')",
        entrypoint="main",
    ).to_dict()


def _report(poc_finding_id="F1", verdict="confirmed"):
    return LiveTestReport(
        poc_finding_id=poc_finding_id,
        verdict=verdict,
        exit_code=0,
        stdout="",
        stderr="",
        duration_ms=5,
    ).to_dict()


def test_gateresult_shape():
    res = gate_transition({"findings": [_finding()]}, "hunt", "triage")
    assert isinstance(res, GateResult)
    assert hasattr(res, "ok") and hasattr(res, "error")
    assert isinstance(res.ok, bool)


# --- hunt -> triage --------------------------------------------------------

def test_hunt_to_triage_passes_with_valid_finding():
    res = gate_transition({"findings": [_finding()]}, "hunt", "triage")
    assert res.ok is True


def test_hunt_to_triage_fails_with_zero_findings():
    res = gate_transition({"findings": []}, "hunt", "triage")
    assert res.ok is False
    assert res.error  # specific, non-empty diagnostic


def test_hunt_to_triage_fails_with_missing_findings_key():
    # Edge case: absent key is treated as empty -> fail.
    res = gate_transition({}, "hunt", "triage")
    assert res.ok is False
    assert res.error


# --- triage -> poc ---------------------------------------------------------

def test_triage_to_poc_passes_with_deduped_findings():
    res = gate_transition(
        {"findings": [_finding("F1"), _finding("F2")]}, "triage", "poc"
    )
    assert res.ok is True


def test_triage_to_poc_fails_on_duplicate_finding_ids():
    # Edge case: duplicate ids are not deduped -> fail.
    res = gate_transition(
        {"findings": [_finding("F1"), _finding("F1")]}, "triage", "poc"
    )
    assert res.ok is False
    assert res.error


# --- poc -> detonate -------------------------------------------------------

def test_poc_to_detonate_passes_when_every_poc_maps_to_finding():
    rows = {
        "findings": [_finding("F1"), _finding("F2")],
        "pocs": [_poc("F1"), _poc("F2")],
    }
    res = gate_transition(rows, "poc", "detonate")
    assert res.ok is True


def test_poc_to_detonate_fails_on_orphan_poc():
    rows = {
        "findings": [_finding("F1")],
        "pocs": [_poc("F1"), _poc("ORPHAN")],
    }
    res = gate_transition(rows, "poc", "detonate")
    assert res.ok is False
    assert res.error


# --- detonate -> report ----------------------------------------------------

def test_detonate_to_report_passes_when_every_poc_has_report():
    rows = {
        "findings": [_finding("F1"), _finding("F2")],
        "pocs": [_poc("F1"), _poc("F2")],
        "reports": [_report("F1"), _report("F2")],
    }
    res = gate_transition(rows, "detonate", "report")
    assert res.ok is True


def test_detonate_to_report_fails_when_a_poc_lacks_report():
    rows = {
        "findings": [_finding("F1"), _finding("F2")],
        "pocs": [_poc("F1"), _poc("F2")],
        "reports": [_report("F1")],  # F2 has no report
    }
    res = gate_transition(rows, "detonate", "report")
    assert res.ok is False
    assert res.error

```

Multiple findings with duplicate IDs during triage -> poc transition: returns GateResult(ok=False, error='Duplicate findings detected')

tasks.title: session_db: normalized SQLite session store with injected path, WAL pragmas, FK/CHECK
acceptance_criteria: New whole-file ngv2/session_db.py defines SessionDB(db_path) taking an injected path with NO hardcoded /tmp default, following the WorkerRegistry(db_path) convention.
Schema creates session_pipeline, findings, pocs, live_test_reports, and phase_validation_logs with FK constraints and CHECK constraints matching contracts.SEVERITIES and contracts.VERDICTS.
Connection setup issues PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000; PRAGMA journal_mode returns 'wal'.
Insert helpers wrap writes in BEGIN IMMEDIATE; insert/fetch round-trips for Finding/PoC/LiveTestReport reproduce the artifact faithfully via contracts to_dict/from_dict.
A bad severity (CHECK violation) and an orphan finding_id (FK violation) are both rejected by the database.

spec.objective: Implement the durable, crash-resilient session-state layer as its own SQLite file (never merged into worker_registry.db/agent_registry/work_intents). SessionDB persists findings, PoCs, detonation/live-test reports, and a phase-validation audit log, with a normalized schema enforcing severity/verdict CHECKs and referential integrity via FKs, and with WAL/busy_timeout pragmas to reduce SQLITE_BUSY.
functional_requirements: SessionDB(db_path) accepts an injected path with no hardcoded default (mirror ngv2/worker_registry.py:46 WorkerRegistry(db_path) convention); the DB lives in its own file.

_init_schema creates session_pipeline, findings, pocs, live_test_reports, phase_validation_logs with FOREIGN KEY constraints (pocs.finding_id -> findings.id, live_test_reports.poc_finding_id -> pocs.finding_id) and CHECK constraints matching contracts.SEVERITIES ('low','medium','high','critical') and contracts.VERDICTS ('confirmed','refuted','error','inconclusive').
Connection setup issues PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000, and PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON so FK constraints are enforced.
Write paths are wrapped in BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions for atomic, gated phase persistence.

Provide insert/fetch round-trip helpers per artifact type (Finding, PoC, LiveTestReport) built on the contracts' existing to_dict/from_dict — no parallel to_row/from_row unless a column shape genuinely requires it.
FK and CHECK violations raise (a bad severity or an orphan finding_id is rejected at write time).
spec.interfaces: SessionDB(db_path: str | os.PathLike). Methods such as insert_finding(Finding)->id, get_finding(id)->Finding, insert_poc(PoC), get_poc(finding_id)->PoC, insert_live_test_report(LiveTestReport), get_live_test_report(poc_finding_id)->LiveTestReport, plus a phase_validation_logs append/fetch. Reuses contracts to_dict/from_dict for row (de)serialization. May reuse B1's GateResult shape conceptually but does not import session_gate.
edge_cases: Inserting a Finding with severity outside SEVERITIES is rejected by the CHECK constraint.
Inserting a PoC whose finding_id has no matching findings row is rejected by the FK constraint (orphan).
After connect, PRAGMA journal_mode returns 'wal' and busy_timeout reflects 5000.
Insert-then-fetch of a Finding/PoC/LiveTestReport yields an object equal to the original (faithful round-trip).
spec.non_goals: No HTTP/REST/MCP server, no network or LLM call, and no integration that physically merges into worker_registry.db/agent_registry/work_intents (separate session DB file; ATTACH DATABASE only if a cross-DB read is ever needed). Does not reconcile the pre-existing three-way intent-table schema collision. Makes no provable concurrency guarantee — WAL/busy_timeout are documented, not unit-asserted as a concurrency proof.

transition_with_gate moves machine to `to` only when gate_result.ok is truthy AND (machine.state.phase, to) is in ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS; a passing gate does NOT bypass the allow-map.

The wrapper is additive and must not alter any existing state_machine symbol.
functional_requirements: Define a new top-level function transition_with_gate(machine, to, gate_result) in ngv2/state_machine.py.
Transition machine to `to` only when gate_result.ok is truthy AND (machine.state.phase, to) is present in ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.
On a failed gate (ok falsy) or a disallowed move, raise ValueError(gate_result.error) and leave machine.state.phase unchanged.

spec.interfaces: transition_with_gate(machine: HuntStateMachine, to: str, gate_result) -> machine (or None); raises ValueError on a failed gate or disallowed transition. gate_result is any object exposing .ok and .error (GateResult shape from B1, duck-typed).

Passing gate AND allowed move advances machine.state.phase to `to`.
